basics.name: Ayomide Emmanuel Abikoye
basics.label: Computer Science Undergraduate · Full-Stack & Backend Developer
basics.summary: Computer Science student at Academic City University (CWA 83.14) with internship experience across three of Ghana's largest banks. I build secure full-stack web apps with React, Next.js and Supabase, write backend services in Java Spring Boot, and enjoy real-time 3D graphics with Three.js. I care about security, data integrity and software that holds up in regulated, high-stakes environments.

work.name: Access Bank Ghana
work.summary: 5-week rotation across Security, Domain & Collab, Hardware, Networking, Infrastructure, Enterprise Apps, Dev Support and Database units.
highlights: Deployed a Jellyfin media server in a virtualized Oracle Linux 10 environment on Oracle VirtualBox to demonstrate Linux server administration.
Provisioned new laptops through Windows Active Directory, joined them to the bank's domain and dispatched them to branches while providing first-line IT support.
Assisted with troubleshooting the Flexcube core banking software, shadowed database administrators and handled secure transfer of physical backup drives for disaster recovery.
Gained exposure to CI/CD, GitOps, containerization, Infrastructure as Code, subnetting and enterprise router configuration.

work.name: Ecobank Ghana (eProcess)
work.summary: Joined the Software Center backend team building services for Ecobank's pan-African digital banking platforms.
highlights: Built RESTful APIs in Java Spring Boot and presented mini-projects to senior developers.
Engineered standardized exception handling that maps system errors to precise financial error codes instead of generic responses.
Mapped Java domain models to PostgreSQL with Spring Data JPA and Hibernate, enforcing data integrity through Spring's transaction management.
Implemented stateless JWT authentication and role-based access control with Spring Security; wrote unit and integration tests with JUnit and Mockito.
Tested production systems, including the Ecobank Mobile App and a POS system, to verify transactions processed correctly.

work.name: Stanbic Bank Ghana
highlights: Collaborated with the programming team to debug and test software applications, ensuring high code quality.
Researched software improvements and compiled detailed project reports.

work.name: Morning Star High School
highlights: Provided technical support and troubleshooting for school computers.
Assisted in the procurement of new computer systems for the school.
Performed software updates and maintenance to extend the life of the school's computers.
Directed a 12-member team to build an interactive, web-based 3D ATM simulation in Three.js, managing the timeline and component integration.
Engineered the 3D scene architecture with custom geometry, complex lighting and raycasting for precise interaction.
Optimized rendering performance by reducing draw calls and managing asset loading for high frame rates across devices.

leadership.position: Project Lead · License Plate Detection ML Model
highlights: Led a 5-member team designing and testing a computer vision app for automated license plate recognition.
Managed the data pipeline, analyzing model metrics to iteratively optimize training and image pre-processing.
Integrated bounding-box overlays and real-time visual feedback, translating model output into UI coordinates.

projects.name: Secure Analytics Pro
highlights: Full-stack analytics platform with a secure CSV/JSON processing engine and real-time visualization dashboard.
JWT authentication and Supabase Row Level Security for strict per-user data isolation.
Containerized monorepo with automated dependency management, scoring 100% on GitHub security audits.

projects.name: Secure ATM Interface Simulator
highlights: Modular 3D environment in React Three Fiber with custom GLSL shaders implementing Phong and Gouraud lighting.
Low-level graphics algorithms from scratch: Bresenham's line, cubic Bézier curves and Cohen–Sutherland clipping.
Finite state machine handling secure PIN entry, authentication and cash withdrawal.
Spatial audio and keyframe animation driven by manual 4×4 matrix transformations.

projects.name: PlateSight: License Plate Detection
highlights: Two YOLO11 detectors trained on a cloud GPU with a reproducible PyTorch/Ultralytics pipeline: 0.87–0.89 mAP@50 on 2,065 held-out real-world photos and 0.95 on Ghanaian plates it never trained on.
Runs entirely in the browser: ONNX Runtime Web in a Web Worker on multi-threaded WebAssembly, with nothing uploaded.
Every compression option passes an accuracy gate on two test sets: INT8 was rejected (up to 10 points lost), float16 weights halved downloads with no loss.
Live webcam detection and one-click plate redaction for privacy-safe sharing, scoring 100 on Lighthouse accessibility, best practices and SEO.
